reference.source: Rook's Textbook of Dermatology / Neurocutaneous Disorders (current reference texts)
clinicalPearls: An umbrella term for disorders in which an epidermal naevus is associated with extracutaneous, chiefly neurological, ocular and skeletal, anomalies
The epidermal naevi follow the lines of Blaschko as verrucous, hyperpigmented streaks reflecting cutaneous mosaicism
Distinct subtypes exist, driven by different mosaic variants (for example FGFR3 or PIK3CA in keratinocytic naevi, HRAS/KRAS in sebaceous/organoid forms)
Neurological involvement includes seizures, developmental delay and hemimegalencephaly, particularly in extensive keratinocytic disease
Ocular findings such as lipodermoids and colobomas and skeletal findings such as scoliosis and limb asymmetry may coexist
Hypophosphataemic rickets from tumour-induced FGF23 excess is a recognised, treatable metabolic association
Management is generic and multidisciplinary: antiseizure therapy, developmental support, and laser or surgical treatment of symptomatic naevi
reference.pathophysiology: Epidermal naevus syndrome results from post-zygotic mosaic variants affecting epidermal progenitor cells during embryogenesis. Depending on the affected gene and cell lineage, the variant produces a keratinocytic, sebaceous or other organoid naevus distributed along the lines of Blaschko. Several causative variants involve growth-signalling pathways, including FGFR3 and PIK3CA in keratinocytic naevi and RAS-pathway genes in sebaceous forms. When the mosaic clone also contributes to neuroectodermal, ocular or mesenchymal tissues, the corresponding brain, eye and skeletal malformations arise, giving the syndrome its characteristic multisystem pattern.
additionalDifferentials: Isolated epidermal or naevus sebaceus without systemic features
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy to characterise the type of epidermal naevus
MRI of the brain for hemimegalencephaly and structural anomalies
MRA when an intracranial vascular malformation is suspected
Ophthalmological review for choristomas and colobomas
Serum phosphate and skeletal survey to detect hypophosphataemic rickets and scoliosis
Molecular analysis of lesional tissue for mosaic variants where available
redFlags: Progressive neurological deficit or developmental regression
Rapid growth, ulceration or nodularity within a naevus
Unexplained bone pain or fractures suggesting hypophosphataemic rickets
reference.prognosis: Outcome is governed by the extent of extracutaneous disease; limited cutaneous involvement carries an excellent prognosis, while extensive neurological disease with intractable seizures and cognitive impairment is associated with greater morbidity.
pitfalls: Treating an extensive epidermal naevus as cosmetic without screening for systemic involvement
Missing hypophosphataemic rickets as a correctable cause of skeletal symptoms
Failing to recognise that the syndrome comprises several genetically distinct subtypes
Delaying neuroimaging in a child with an extensive naevus and seizures
references: Happle R. Mosaicism in Human Skin
management: No cure exists; symptomatic epidermal naevi are treated with topical keratolytics or retinoids, laser ablation, or surgical excision where they cause functional or cosmetic problems
Control seizures with antiseizure medication, and consider epilepsy surgery or hemispherectomy for drug-resistant focal seizures arising from hemimegalencephaly
Correct tumour-induced hypophosphataemic rickets with oral phosphate and active vitamin D (calcitriol), with FGF23-directed therapy where available
Provide developmental support, physiotherapy and educational input for delay, and orthopaedic management of scoliosis and limb-length asymmetry
Arrange ophthalmological care for choristomas and colobomas, and periodic surveillance of serum phosphate, brain imaging and the spine for evolving complications
Coordinate care through a multidisciplinary team spanning dermatology, neurology, ophthalmology, orthopaedics and clinical genetics
Offer genetic counselling explaining the post-zygotic mosaic basis and generally low recurrence risk
